findings.evidence: kit.py _verify_substitute_identity requires ASSIGNMENT.launch to be the complete {path,sha256} reference to LAUNCH.json; LAUNCH.worker_result is the complete reference to the actual candidate .agent-workspace/RESULT.json; _verify_c3_completion then requires that actual RESULT.json contain exactly one PASS check whose command is ASSIGNMENT.json's raw sha256.
findings.observed: The required dependency graph is ASSIGNMENT.sha256 -> RESULT.check.command -> LAUNCH.worker_result.sha256 -> LAUNCH.sha256 -> ASSIGNMENT.launch.sha256 -> ASSIGNMENT.sha256. _write_new makes the limitation artifacts create-once, and the lane controller validates RESULT.json only after the worker exits, so no first artifact can be written without changing the hash required by an already-written predecessor.
findings.expected: A real C3 substitute must be creatable in one pass: a pre-run immutable assignment must not hash-reference future launch or result artifacts; the worker RESULT may credit that assignment hash; post-run launch/execution/result adapters may then reference the completed real status/result.
findings.reproduction: Construct the required substitute artifacts in dependency order. Writing ASSIGNMENT first is impossible because its required launch sha256 is unknown. Writing LAUNCH first is impossible because its required actual RESULT sha256 is unknown. Writing RESULT first is impossible because its required firmware-limitation-credit command is ASSIGNMENT's unknown sha256. Any later rewrite violates create-once/hash validation.
findings.impact: No real C3-HARNESS substitute can satisfy the verifier, so an otherwise valid proved server limitation cannot receive substitute credit or produce an authorized limitation record.
findings.no_fix_consequence: The limitation path remains non-executable and will fail closed for every real substitute, defeating the intended strongest-safe fallback.
findings.smallest_fix: Split the substitute proof into a pre-run ASSIGNMENT with no LAUNCH or actual-result hash, a real worker RESULT that credits ASSIGNMENT.sha256, and post-run LAUNCH/EXECUTION/limitation RESULT adapters that reference the completed real status/result and assignment.
findings.alternatives: Remove the credit binding (weaker evidence), or redesign the artifact schemas around the acyclic order described above (preferred).
findings.cost_benefit: The redesign is localized to limitation evidence schemas and verifier tests, while it restores an otherwise impossible production fallback path.

findings.evidence: kit.py passes canonical_sha256(attribution value) as the required firmware-limitation-credit token to _verify_c3_completion. The attribution value contains diagnostic_execution as a complete {path,sha256} reference to DIAGNOSTIC.json; DIAGNOSTIC.json contains worker_result as a complete reference to the actual diagnostic .agent-workspace/RESULT.json.
findings.observed: The required dependency graph is ATTRIBUTION.sha256 -> diagnostic RESULT.check.command -> DIAGNOSTIC.worker_result.sha256 -> DIAGNOSTIC.sha256 -> ATTRIBUTION.diagnostic_execution.sha256 -> ATTRIBUTION.sha256. Thus the claimed causal pinned-component diagnostic cannot be emitted create-once before, during, or after its actual C3 execution.
findings.expected: A diagnostic assignment/attribution seed must exist before diagnostic execution without hashing future execution evidence; the actual validated diagnostic RESULT may credit that seed; a post-run diagnostic adapter and final attribution may reference the completed artifacts without being the token the worker had to know in advance.
findings.reproduction: Attempt to produce attribution, DIAGNOSTIC.json, and the actual candidate RESULT.json. Attribution cannot be finalized before DIAGNOSTIC's sha256, DIAGNOSTIC cannot be finalized before RESULT's sha256, and RESULT cannot be validated before it contains the final attribution canonical sha256. Rewriting any artifact changes the referenced digest and is rejected.
findings.impact: No causal pinned-component reproduction can pass verification, so the only path capable of proving a pinned-server limitation is unavailable.
findings.no_fix_consequence: Every limitation decision requiring the mandated diagnostic evidence fails closed; the added causal proof cannot be used in a real deployment.
findings.smallest_fix: Introduce a pre-run diagnostic assignment whose hash is the worker credit token and which excludes future result/adapter hashes. After PASS, write diagnostic execution and final attribution adapters that bind the completed real result, source/input/failure signatures, and assignment.
findings.alternatives: Drop the exact worker credit requirement (weaker), or use the pre-run diagnostic-assignment DAG (preferred).
findings.cost_benefit: A small evidence-schema sequencing change makes the new causal requirement executable; leaving it cyclic makes the feature unusable.

findings.evidence: _verify_c3_completion requires the result reference to equal declaration.worktree_root/.agent-workspace/RESULT.json, but for controller_status it only requires that .agent-workspace be an ancestor of the supplied path. lane_controller writes terminal state to the configurable invocation output_paths.status path; that configured path is neither carried by the status payload nor compared by the verifier.
findings.observed: Any separately created JSON file under the candidate worktree's .agent-workspace can be supplied as controller_status if it has a static terminal-status shape consistent with the real RESULT.json. Its pid/creation fields then become the derived c3_controller identity even though it need not be the lane controller's configured terminal status artifact.
findings.expected: The verifier must bind controller_status to the exact configured terminal-status path for the candidate invocation, while continuing to use the real .agent-workspace/RESULT.json path recorded by result_validation.
findings.reproduction: Use a real candidate RESULT.json and copy or synthesize a schema-conforming CODEX_EXITED status JSON at another filename under the same .agent-workspace. The current path predicate accepts that alternate file; no equality check identifies the configured output_paths.status file.
findings.impact: The repaired controller identity and terminal-status provenance remain selectable rather than demonstrated, weakening the C3 evidence that is meant to be tied to the actual candidate lane controller.
findings.no_fix_consequence: A limitation artifact can be accepted using a workspace-local status surrogate instead of the real terminal status, despite the new real-result binding.
findings.smallest_fix: Record the resolved configured status path in the controller status or in an immutable pre-run C3 assignment/invocation reference, then require controller_status.path to equal that exact value; keep future hashes out of the pre-run artifact.
findings.alternatives: Treat any in-workspace status-shaped file as sufficient (current behavior), or add a self/path binding to the candidate controller contract (preferred).
findings.cost_benefit: This is a narrow equality check that completes the real-status correction and protects the controller identity on which substitute and diagnostic evidence rely.
